top.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
top.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Read more Physics of light and magnetism rewritten after almost two centuries Because the rotor experiences essentially no friction, and it is magnetic and cold, its behaviour is very sensitive to its environment, which makes it a promising sensor. The team has already successfully tested it as a gauge of vacuum at very low temperatures. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Benjamin Stickler at Ulm University in Germany says the levitated spinning magnet could also be used to precisely sense and measure magnetic fields. top.title: An unexpected feedback loop may be driving mega heatwaves
top.description: Land scorched by a fire in Wennington, London, during the record-breaking heatwave in 2022 Shutterstock Mid-latitude regions such as Europe are set to suffer more intense heatwaves than previously thought, according to new research that has uncovered a three-way feedback loop that amplifies extreme heat conditions. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? In the UK in 2022, temperatures exceeded 40°C (104 ° F) for the first time in history, despite predictions that such a milestone was probably still years away. Likewise, the 2021 heatwave in the Pacific Northwest saw temperatures hit extremes that far outstripped climate model projections. Advertisement Researchers have been scrambling to understand why very extreme heat is occurring more frequently, and with greater intensity, than expected at this level of warming. One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land. They also knew that higher temperatures dry soils more quickly, removing the cooling effect provided by evaporation, thereby further amplifying heatwaves. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Now it seems that when temperatures climb high enough, dry soil, high pressure and extreme heat can amplify each other further, with dry soil helping to sustain high-pressure systems in the atmosphere. “Basically, the soils that are affected by circulation pattern also start to affect back on the circulation pattern itself,” says Kai Kornhuber at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis in Austria. This three-way feedback effect makes extreme heatwaves 10 per cent hotter than they would otherwise be, according to the research by Kornhuber and his colleagues – a factor not fully accounted for in climate model projections. This will have serious consequences for our ability to cope with future extreme heat. “Ten per cent hotter or colder can really make a difference between a heatwave and a record-shattering heatwave,” says Kornhuber. “We’re facing so many critical thresholds in social and biophysical systems that an extra 10 per cent can really lead to temperatures that are then quite damaging.” Read more Is a broken jet stream causing extreme weather that lasts longer? This may include serious public health consequences, a breakdown of vital infrastructure such as transport links and energy grids, crop failures and the collapse of ecosystems. top.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
top.description: With Earth & Sky, her Spring/Summer 2027 collection , Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis. The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A Cycle Of Giving Back In nature, nothing is wasted and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back.That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. top.title: Golfers Gain Distance By Fixing Attack Angle Numbers
top.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Most avid golfers track their swing speed, yet many ignore the single metric that changes distance the most. Attack angle determines whether the club moves up or down at the moment of impact. This number dictates launch height and spin rates more than almost any other factor in the game. According to MyGolfSpy , a positive angle means the club moves upward, while a negative angle indicates a downward strike. The ideal number differs completely between the driver and irons, a fact that often confuses players who try to hit every club the same way. Understanding this distinction allows a golfer to maximize carry distance without increasing swing speed. MyGolfSpy reports that inconsistent attack angles can cause high-handicap players to see over 30 yards of carry variation. The same golfer with the same speed can hit shots 12 yards apart just by changing the angle of attack. This gap exists because the club path interacts with the ball differently depending on whether it is teed up or sitting on the turf. The Driver Requires an Upward Strike With the driver, the goal is to hit the ball on an upward strike. Golfers should tee the ball high and position it toward the front of the stance to facilitate this motion. MyGolfSpy explains that hitting up helps in two specific ways: it launches the ball higher and reduces spin. High launch combined with low spin creates the optimal conditions for maximum distance. Data provided by GOLFJOY and cited by MyGolfSpy shows a clear difference when comparing a -5 degree angle to a +5 degree angle. When a golfer swings at 80 mph, hitting down on the ball produces a lower trajectory with excessive spin that kills distance. Conversely, hitting up with a +5 degree angle optimizes the launch conditions. Reports note that the same swing speed yields vastly different results based solely on this vertical club path. Players who try to hit down on the driver are fighting the physics of the club design. Irons Demand a Slight Downward Angle Irons work in the opposite direction compared to the driver. The ball sits on the ground, so the club must strike the ball first and then the turf. This sequence ensures clean contact and proper spin to hold the green. MyGolfSpy states that the sweet spot for a 7-iron is roughly 2 to 5 degrees downward. Striking the ball with too little or too much downward angle costs significant distance. An 80 mph swing with a -4 degree angle produces a launch of 18 degrees, which represents the middle option that wins for most players. Deviating from this range leads to poor contact. If the angle is too flat, the club may catch the turf before the ball. If the angle is too steep, the player might thin the shot or lose energy transfer. The data shows that the middle option within the 2 to 5 degree range consistently delivers the best results for carry and control. top.title: Military force alone cannot defeat terrorism – Buratai
top.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Tukur Buratai (retd.), has said that military force alone cannot defeat terrorism in Nigeria, stressing the need to address poverty, unemployment, poor governance and other socio-economic factors fuelling insecurity. Buratai, who spoke on Friday in Lagos at the public presentation of a book, Beyond Military Force: A Strategy for Countering Terrorism in Nigeria, said although military operations remained essential in confronting armed groups, sustainable peace could only be achieved through a combination of military and non-military interventions. The former army chief, who served between 2015 and 2021, described the book as an important intellectual contribution to Nigeria’s counter-terrorism efforts, noting that security challenges in the North-East and North-West required a comprehensive strategy beyond the use of weapons. “Military force, however professional, is a shield, not a substitute for governance. It can create the conditions for peace, but it cannot by itself build peace. “It can degrade a terrorist group; it cannot alone remove the grievances of poverty, ignorance and manipulation from which such groups recruit,” he said. Buratai emphasised the importance of intelligence gathering and community participation in counter-insurgency operations, describing local communities as indispensable partners in the fight against terrorism. According to him, security agencies cannot achieve meaningful results without the confidence and cooperation of the communities they are deployed to protect. “No amount of firepower can compensate for poor intelligence. The community is often the best source of intelligence, but only when the community trusts the security agencies,” he stated. He also warned that human rights violations during military operations could alienate local communities and provide terrorist organisations with propaganda materials to attract new recruits. Buratai disclosed that the Nigerian Army reviewed its rules of engagement during his tenure to ensure compliance with prevailing standards, while introducing human rights desks and other accountability mechanisms. He called for stronger counter-terrorism capacity within the Nigeria Police Force, arguing that the military should not continue to shoulder responsibilities traditionally assigned to civilian security institutions. “The military is not the police; it is not the social welfare agency; it is not the school system. When the military is deployed to perform tasks that belong to civil authorities, it becomes overstretched, and the roots of the conflict remain untouched,” he said. top.title: Mets’ Johnny Washington Hire Leaves Braves Fans With Big Questions
top.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The New York Mets just made a move that stings for Atlanta fans. They hired Johnny Washington as a co-hitting coach, pulling him right from the Braves’ organization. Washington served as the Braves’ minor league hitting coordinator during the 2026 season. The Mets are now stacking three hitting coaches in one room, a setup that feels strange for a team that needs immediate offense. A Familiar Name in a New Spot Washington is not a stranger to the Mets. Andy Green, the current Mets manager, previously employed him with the San Diego Padres and subsequently the Chicago Cubs. The hiring was reported by Joel Sherman of the New York Post, who noted the Mets finally have a new coach after weeks of searching. They fired their previous hitting coordinator, Jeff Albert, after just one season in the role. Washington joins Troy Snitker and Rafael Fernandez. The situation looks odd because the Mets missed out on top targets. Prior to selecting Washington, they consulted John Mallee of the Chicago Cubs and Kevin Long of the Philadelphia Phillies. Each was considered a top contender to direct the staff. Instead, the Mets turned to a familiar voice from Green’s past. This choice suggests they could not land the big names they wanted. The Braves, meanwhile, kept Tim Hyers as their hitting coach despite a lackluster offensive season. Why the Braves Let Him Go Braves fans have to ask why Washington slipped through their fingers. The team kept Hyers even though the offense ranked eighth in runs but had the third-fewest walks in MLB. Their on-base percentage of .309 was a full point lower than the Mets. In 2026, only the Colorado Rockies and San Francisco Giants posted a lower on-base rate than Atlanta. Washington would have signaled a change, but the Braves chose stability over a new voice. Washington’s past has its own baggage, though. He was the hitting coach for the Los Angeles Angels when they posted poor numbers. In 2024, the Angels batted .226 with him. Year two saw them hit .225. Before his Angels departure, a Reddit discussion noted an interview regarding his hitting philosophy. Critics labeled him a home run enthusiast who promoted a “wait for your pitch and end the at-bat” philosophy, according to Rising Apple . The Mets hired a coach with a mixed track record. The Mets cannot afford to repeat their offensive struggles from last season. They ranked in the bottom 10 in on-base percentage, slugging percentage, and runs scored. With Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto back healthy, the offense must improve. The Brewers had four hitting coaches last season and won the World Series. Milwaukee utilized a lead coach, whereas the Mets allegedly lack such a role currently.

top.title: Jessica Pegula jokes about 'hot mic' incident at WTA Finals media day
top.description: American tennis star Jessica Pegula wasted little time defusing the tension around the well-documented "hot mic" incident during her appearance with media Friday ahead of the WTA Finals. As Pegula entered the room and sat down at the front of the press conference, she grabbed the microphone and playfully tapped it and said "OK, the mic's on. Just wanted to be sure." Her joke drew a laugh from the assembled media. Pegula was referencing an incident that happened earlier in the week when a microphone on the practice court that was intended to just pick up ambient noise of tennis balls hitting the hardcourt and environmental sounds for a livestream, actually picked up a conversation between Pegula and one of her coaches during a practice session. On the live stream she was heard calling another tour player Mirra Andreeva a "diva" among other comments in what she thought was a private discussion. A spokesperson for Pegula has since reported that Pegula "had absolutely no idea that her conversation with (her coach) was being livestreamed and certainly never expected a private discussion during practice to be made public." Pegula has since apologized to the other players involved. For its part, the WTA has taken full responsibility and apologized to Pegula for the incident. On Friday, WTA Chair Valerie Camillo, who spoke to the media minutes before Pegula did, struck a different tone that Pegula's light-hearted opener. She was quite serious. She said livestreaming practices is an attempt to bring fans closer to the game and they have done it before, using the similar ambient noise effect, but in this case mistakes were made. "There were several breakdowns in our execution of the livestream, given our own policies and procedures. There was a lack of advanced notice and clear signage to assist players about the recording equipment operating in the area and it was also not our intention to capture conversations on the livestream of practices but rather to record ambient sound. So clearly there was a failure in our technical execution. As the chair of the WTA I'm committed to leading an organization that delivers the best for our players, our tournaments and our fans. Our execution here did not meet that standard," she said. "I want to specifically apologize to Jessica Pegula, what happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest start and she does not deserve this distraction. One of the primary responsibilities of the WTA is to protect our players whenever possible. ANd that did not happen here. Players deserve better and we will continue to work to raise the bar at the WTA." Camillo went on to say that the sound has been disabled now on the practice courts for the rest of this event. top.title: Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles' injury shakes up clash against Iowa
top.description: The big Iowa -Northwestern matchup got a Friday surprise, one day before the Nov. 7 kickoff at Ryan Field (6:30 p.m., FOX). ESPN’s Pete Thamel reported that star Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles, who had been listed as questionable on the first two injury reports of the week, will miss the game against the Hawkeyes with an upper-body injury. Nicco Marchiol, a left-handed transfer from West Virginia who has attempted one pass this season, is expected to make the start against an Iowa defense that ranks No. 4 nationally. Veteran back-up Nicco Marchiol will make the start for Northwestern, his first start for the Wildcats. He’s a veteran who has a 6-2 record as a starter while at West Virginia. He’s played in 27 career games. — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) November 6, 2026 The sudden move shifted the betting line. Iowa went from a 2½-point underdog to a 2½-point favorite as of early Friday afternoon. The 19th-ranked Hawkeyes (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten Conference) spoke earlier this week about wanting to atone for a poor 2024 performance against Chiles when he was with Michigan State and dominated Iowa, 32-20, in East Lansing. Chiles had been playing fantastic football, having thrown 13 touchdowns and rushed for 10 more with just one interception through eight games this fall. He has been the catalyst for Chip Kelly’s unique offense that catered to his dual-threat capabilities. And while it is seemingly a benefit for Iowa to face Northwestern (6-2, 3-2) without its star quarterback, it does throw a lot of preparations made all week into the trash can. While Northwestern probably won’t change its style of offense, Marchiol does bring a less-mobile presence to the field. But he does have experience. Marchiol started seven games during his four seasons at West Virginia, including the first four of 2025 before suffering a season-ending foot injury. He completed 66 of 98 passes (67.3%) for 720 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions last season while posting a 3-1 record for the Mountaineers. Iowa is coming off a 30-0 home shutout of then-No. 25 Wisconsin at Kinnick Stadium and needs to win its final four regular-season games to have a shot at the College Football Playoff. This bit of quarterback news would seem to help the cause, at least a little bit. Hawkeyes columnist Chad Leistikow has served for 32 years with The Des Moines Register and USA TODAY Sports Network. nigeria.title: Military force alone cannot defeat terrorism – Buratai
nigeria.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Tukur Buratai (retd.), has said that military force alone cannot defeat terrorism in Nigeria, stressing the need to address poverty, unemployment, poor governance and other socio-economic factors fuelling insecurity. Buratai, who spoke on Friday in Lagos at the public presentation of a book, Beyond Military Force: A Strategy for Countering Terrorism in Nigeria, said although military operations remained essential in confronting armed groups, sustainable peace could only be achieved through a combination of military and non-military interventions. The former army chief, who served between 2015 and 2021, described the book as an important intellectual contribution to Nigeria’s counter-terrorism efforts, noting that security challenges in the North-East and North-West required a comprehensive strategy beyond the use of weapons. “Military force, however professional, is a shield, not a substitute for governance. It can create the conditions for peace, but it cannot by itself build peace. “It can degrade a terrorist group; it cannot alone remove the grievances of poverty, ignorance and manipulation from which such groups recruit,” he said. Buratai emphasised the importance of intelligence gathering and community participation in counter-insurgency operations, describing local communities as indispensable partners in the fight against terrorism. According to him, security agencies cannot achieve meaningful results without the confidence and cooperation of the communities they are deployed to protect. “No amount of firepower can compensate for poor intelligence. The community is often the best source of intelligence, but only when the community trusts the security agencies,” he stated. He also warned that human rights violations during military operations could alienate local communities and provide terrorist organisations with propaganda materials to attract new recruits. Buratai disclosed that the Nigerian Army reviewed its rules of engagement during his tenure to ensure compliance with prevailing standards, while introducing human rights desks and other accountability mechanisms. He called for stronger counter-terrorism capacity within the Nigeria Police Force, arguing that the military should not continue to shoulder responsibilities traditionally assigned to civilian security institutions. “The military is not the police; it is not the social welfare agency; it is not the school system. When the military is deployed to perform tasks that belong to civil authorities, it becomes overstretched, and the roots of the conflict remain untouched,” he said. nigeria.title: 2027: ADC-PCC vows to sustain campaigns despite leadership crisis
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike Following the filing of an appeal against the Federal High Court judgment on its leadership dispute, the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council has vowed to sustain its campaigns for the 2027 elections, insisting that the crisis will not distract it from its mission or stop its mobilisation across the country. The council is determined to keep its political machinery running and its message before Nigerians, even as it battles to protect party’s leadership structure from the fallout of the November 5 judgment. In a statement on Friday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the party disclosed that it had also applied for a stay of execution of the judgment involving Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe and the ADC. It said the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, was formally notified of the appeal and stay application on November 6. The ADC urged INEC to exercise restraint and refrain from taking any consequential action on the party’s leadership while the legal challenge remained pending. Appealing to members, supporters and Nigerians, Shaibu urged them not to lose confidence in the party or its political project. “To our members, supporters and Nigerians who believe in democracy: remain calm, steadfast and confident. This is not the end of the road. The ADC is taking every lawful step to defend its rights, and we will not be intimidated or distracted from that responsibility,” he said. The campaign council insisted that the leadership dispute would not interrupt its political activities or its engagement with Nigerians. “Our campaigns continue without interruption. There is no stopping the affordability train or our mission to make life better for Nigerians. We will keep taking our message to the people as we pursue every lawful avenue to defend our rights,” Shaibu stated. The council expressed confidence that the dispute would receive a full hearing, maintaining that it would continue to pursue all lawful avenues to defend its interests. nigeria.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
nigeria.description: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday. So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases have been reported across the country of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation’s leading public health agency. That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991. State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children. Measles was declared eradicated from the United States in 2000 thanks to vaccination, but in recent years it has made a strong comeback, fueled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities. President Donald Trump’s Health Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. is accused of fanning that distrust. He is known for his vaccine skepticism and has repeatedly disseminated misinformation about the measles vaccine and downplayed the dangers of the disease. Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death. Before the vaccine was developed in the early 1960s, measles killed hundreds of children each year in the US. It continues to claim tens of thousands of lives worldwide. nigeria.title: Mbappe headlines Zidane’s France squad, Pagis gets call-up
nigeria.description: Kylian Mbappe headlined the France squad named Friday by coach Zinedine Zidane for their Nations League matches against Italy and Turkey after picking up an injury on international duty in September, while Pablo Pagis was handed a debut call-up. Real Madrid superstar Mbappe, the France captain, scored the winner in Zidane’s first match in charge of Les Bleus away to Turkey on September 25, but suffered a knee injury in the same game that ruled him out of the team’s three remaining fixtures of the last international window. Without him, France won twice against Belgium, in Brussels and then at home, and drew in between against Italy. Mbappe has since returned to action for his club, scoring eight times in seven matches between La Liga and the Champions League. France are without Paris Saint-Germain star Ousmane Dembele and Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul for this month’s double-header, so Marcus Thuram of Inter Milan is recalled to an attack which will also feature Pagis for the first time. The 23-year-old Pagis, who plays chiefly as an attacking midfielder, is rewarded for his impressive form this season since joining Paris FC — who are fourth in Ligue 1 — from Lorient. Pagis is the son of Mickael Pagis, the former Marseille player who at one time appeared for the France beach soccer team coached by Eric Cantona. Aurelien Tchouameni of Real Madrid returns in midfield in place of Manu Kone after missing the last international window, while Manchester United’s Leny Yoro and Chelsea’s Malo Gusto replace Jules Kounde of Barcelona and Maxence Lacroix of Chelsea in the defence. Zidane’s side play Italy in Milan next Thursday, November 12, and then take on Turkey in Bordeaux three days later in their final group-stage fixtures. They are top of Nations League Group A1 with 10 points from four outings, three ahead of Italy. The top two teams in the group will advance to the quarter-finals next March. nigeria.title: Osimhen sustains knee injury, to miss Nigeria’s AFCON qualifiers
nigeria.description: Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen is set to undergo knee surgery after sustaining an injury during Galatasaray’s UEFA Champions League clash against VfB Stuttgart. The Turkish champions confirmed on Friday that the Nigerian forward suffered a strain in his left knee, with an MRI scan revealing a loose body in the affected area. In a statement, Galatasaray said Osimhen would undergo arthroscopic knee surgery on Saturday at Maslak Acıbadem Hospital under the supervision of the club’s doctor, Yener İnce. The statement read: “Our player Victor Osimhen, who suffered a strain in his left knee during our UEFA Champions League match against VfB Stuttgart and was found to have a loose body in MRI scans, is scheduled to undergo arthroscopic knee surgery tomorrow at Maslak Acıbadem Hospital, performed by our club doctor Yener İnce.” The club also confirmed that the 26-year-old had been withdrawn from the squad for its next fixture against Amed S. F. Osimhen’s injury is a major setback for Nigeria, with the striker now expected to miss the Super Eagles’ Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixtures against Tanzania on November 13 and 17. His absence would leave Nigeria without one of its most influential attacking players as the national team prepares for the upcoming international fixtures. The Super Eagles will hope for a successful operation and a quick recovery for the Galatasaray forward, although the club is yet to announce an expected return date.\ Vanguard News The post Osimhen sustains knee injury, to miss Nigeria’s AFCON qualifiers appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: ADC chairmen demand Mark’s removal; threaten protest against INEC
nigeria.description: The National Executive Committee Chairmen Forum of the African Democratic Congress has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission to remove Senator David Mark and members of his dissolved Interim National Working Committee from its portal, threatening a nationwide protest if the commission fails to comply with a court judgment on the party’s leadership crisis. The forum also demanded that INEC replace their names with those of Nafiu Bala Gombe and other party officials it considers legally recognised. It further urged the commission to reopen its portal to allow the ADC to conduct fresh primaries where necessary and upload its candidates for the 2027 general elections. The forum’s secretary, Kennedy Odion, made the demands while addressing journalists in Abuja on Friday, a day after Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, nullified the Mark-led interim leadership of the party. Odion said the judgment invalidated decisions taken by the dissolved leadership, including the nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate and the emergence of other candidates through its congresses and national convention. He said the ruling affirmed the forum’s position that the interim leadership was not constitutionally recognised. “We, the only legally recognised NEC members, accept in its entirety the judgment declaring our own Alhaji Nafiu Bala Gombe the authentic national chairman of the ADC. “Failure to comply with this latest judgment will leave us no option but to proceed with our planned nationwide protest against the electoral umpire. Nigeria is for all of us. No individual, however highly placed, is above the law,” he said. Odion also argued that the judgment invalidated the candidacies of Atiku, his running mate, former Minister of Transportation Rotimi Amaechi, and other politicians who emerged through the interim leadership’s processes. The ADC has been divided by a prolonged leadership dispute between the Mark-led interim national working committee and the faction led by Bala Gombe. The crisis had earlier resulted in a Federal High Court judgment delivered by Justice Joyce Abdulmalik on April 29, 2026, which affirmed the tenure of elected state executive committees pending the conduct of valid congresses and a national convention. The court also restrained INEC from recognising congresses organised by the interim national working committee. The Court of Appeal upheld the decision on June 13, 2026. Odion alleged that despite the earlier rulings, INEC continued to recognise the Mark-led leadership and accept candidates produced through its congresses and convention. He said the forum had pursued legal remedies rather than confrontation, adding that its restraint had prevented violence among aggrieved party members. nigeria.title: I’ll sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight – Tinubu
nigeria.description: By Nwafor Sunday President Bola Tinubu has said he will spend the night in Akwa Ibom State, declaring that his visit is a “second term presidential sleep” as he expressed confidence in securing re-election in 2027. Tinubu made the remark on Friday during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. Addressing the crowd, the President thanked the people of Akwa Ibom for their support and urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 general election. “Thank you, Akwa Ibom. I love you with my heart. I will sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight. It’s going to be a second term presidential sleep. I will dream of victory too. “I will depend on you to go out and vote. The weapon you have is the PVC. If you have not collected it, please go ahead and collect your PVC. I am begging you, for the sake of your future,” he said. Tinubu also reiterated his administration’s promises of improved living conditions, infrastructure development, education, skills acquisition and job creation. “I promised you a better future, I promised you development, I promised you education. I promised you skill development, I promised you jobs. We are going to plant a lot of economic trees,” he added. The President’s declaration comes amid criticism from the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, who had taken a swipe at him over his travels across the country. Obi had suggested that Tinubu had not spent the night in any state outside Abuja and Lagos, a remark that appeared to question the President’s physical presence across the country. Tinubu’s announcement that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom comes against the backdrop of the exchange between the two political figures as political activities ahead of the 2027 general election gather momentum. nigeria.title: Tinubu Approves Ibom Deep-Sea Port, Akwa Ibom International Airport Status
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the proposed Ibom Deep-Sea Port and the upgrade of the Victor Attah International Airport in Akwa Ibom State to international airport status. The President announced the approvals while addressing residents of the state at a rally held in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday He had made a similar promise during his 2023 presidential campaign rally at the same stadium, pledging to establish a deep-sea port in Akwa Ibom. He cited the Lekki Deep Sea Port, developed during his tenure as Lagos State Governor, as a model for the proposed project. Tinubu urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the electoral process. “I heard from my friend, my governor, my pastor, on behalf of the people and leadership of Akwa Ibom, a request for Ibom’s deep-sea port. Ibom Deep-Sea Port. It’s approved,” Tinubu said. The approval came after Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, pledged that the state would deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 if the Federal Government approved and facilitated the delivery of the Ibom Deep-Sea Port project. ﻿ “Give us Ibom Deep Seaport, we will deliver two million votes. This deep seaport is capable of unlocking the economy of the state, the South-South region and Nigeria at large,” Eno said. On infrastructure, the President disclosed that he had approved the request by the state leadership for the Victor Attah International Airport to attain international airport status. He promised a better future for the people of Akwa Ibom, pledging investments in education, skills development, job creation and economic growth. He said his administration would support the development of economic opportunities in the state, particularly through the cultivation and processing of palm produce. “There is no reason why Akwa Ibom cannot use the value of palm trees and the palms here. There is no reason that we cannot create skills, developmental skills, that are enduring and everlasting,” he said. The President said the port would generate economic value and promote development in the state. He stressed that development must be inclusive and capable of creating tangible economic benefits for the people. Tinubu also urged residents to support the state governor, encouraging them to follow his leadership and heed his guidance. nigeria.title: Lagos seals over 45 buildings in Eko, Ifako-Ijaiye
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Physical Planning Permit Authority (LASPPPA) has sealed more than 45 buildings in Eko and Ifako-Ijaiye districts over alleged violations of physical planning regulations. The enforcement exercises were carried out by the authority’s Monitoring and Compliance Unit on Wednesday in Ifako-Ijaiye District and Thursday in Eko District. In a statement shared on its Facebook page on Thursday, LASPPPA said 25 properties were sealed in Ifako-Ijaiye for operating without valid planning permits, excessive density, illegal remodelling, deviation from approved plans and ongoing construction without approval. In a separate update on Friday, the agency disclosed that more than 20 buildings were sealed in Eko District for various planning violations. It said 10 properties were found to have deviated from their approved building plans, while five were sealed for excessive density and another five for carrying out remodelling without the required permits. Other affected properties were sealed for undertaking construction work without planning approval. According to LASPPPA, the affected property owners and developers had earlier been served contravention notices by the respective district offices but failed to comply with the directives. “Contravention notices had been served by the district office previously, but compliance was not achieved,” the agency stated. The authority advised owners and developers of the affected properties to visit their nearest LASPPPA district office or its headquarters at Oba Akinjobi Way, GRA, Ikeja, for regularisation and further guidance. Meanwhile, a source in the agency, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said monitoring and enforcement of physical planning regulations were continuous exercises. nigeria.title: Just in: Tinubu approves Ibom Deep Seaport in Akwa Ibom
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has approved the long-awaited Ibom Deep Seaport project in Akwa Ibom State following a request by Governor Umo Eno. Tinubu announced the approval on Friday while responding to the governor’s appeal during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. The President, who was in the state to inaugurate projects executed by the Eno administration, said development must promote inclusive growth, create economic value and improve the lives of the people. Responding to Eno’s request for the deep seaport, Tinubu said: “Now, development must be even inclusive and reasonable, must bring progress and create economic value. I heard from my friend, my governor, my pastor, on behalf of the people and leadership of Akwa Ibom, request for Ibom’s deep-sea port.” After repeating the request, the President asked the crowd, “Will you vote?” He subsequently declared, “Okay, it’s approved.” The approval followed a pledge by Eno that Akwa Ibom would deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 if the Federal Government approved and delivered the seaport project. “Give us Ibom Deep Seaport, we will deliver two million votes. This deep seaport is capable of unlocking the economy of the state, the South-South region and Nigeria at large,” the governor said. Eno described the project as the most important economic demand of the people of Akwa Ibom, saying it would transform the state’s maritime, industrial and employment sectors. He said the people had remained loyal to Tinubu since 2023 and were asking him to fulfil his earlier promise to establish the facility. Tinubu had, during his 2023 presidential campaign rally at the same stadium, promised to build the deep seaport, citing the Lekki Deep Seaport, developed during his tenure as Lagos State governor, as an example of what he intended to achieve in Akwa Ibom. Eno recalled that the project, originally conceived during the administration of former Governor Victor Attah as the Ibaka Deep Seaport and Industrial City, had remained unrealised for decades despite featuring in successive presidential campaigns. “This seaport would serve as a major transhipment hub. It will create thousands of jobs for our people. It will open Akwa Ibom to international trade and investment,” he said. The governor also said Akwa Ibom had aligned with the Federal Government by joining the All Progressives Congress (APC) to attract greater federal presence and development to the state. He assured Tinubu of the state’s support for his re-election bid in 2027, describing the proposed seaport as a major development expected from the President’s administration. nigeria.title: Kenyan preacher sentenced to 200 years in prison over child murders
nigeria.description: A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday for the murder of 190 children and one adult in an infamous starvation cult. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the sect’s base near the coastal resort of Malindi, in what became known as the “Shakahola Forest Massacre”. Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, was accused of inciting his followers to starve themselves to death to “meet Jesus”. He was convicted last month of murdering 191 people between January 2021 and September 2023, alongside 28 co-accused. On Friday, the court sentenced him to 100 years for the homicide charges and 100 years for the starvation charges, while his accomplices — many of whom starved their own children to death — received a variety of lengthy prison terms. “Children observed siblings drop dead… as their parents ate and drank,” the judge said. “Some died as a result of strangulation, severely beaten… Children were subjected to extreme suffering… terrifying living conditions, psychological trauma.” Mackenzie was impassive as the sentence was read out, as he had been throughout the trial. Prosecutors had called for the death penalty, but the judge said it would “fail to achieve deterrence, particularly where the convicts regard death as a pathway to heaven and a union with Jesus and their deceased children.” Kenya has the death penalty but has not carried out an execution since 1987. Francis Wanje, a 62-year-old teacher who lost two grandchildren to the cult, told AFP he had hoped Mackenzie would be sentenced to death to prevent further tragedies. Another of his grandchildren, now 11, went without food for eight days before being rescued in March 2023. He testified that his brothers, aged two and five, had died after their parents, acting on the guru’s orders, forbade them from eating or drinking. “Nothing can ease the pain,” said Wanje, who blamed authorities for failing to act swiftly. “I really have great (anger) towards the authorities. If they had taken action, we would not be here today,” he added. – Death penalty – Mackenzie’s lawyer said he would appeal the verdict. He also faces manslaughter and terrorism charges in other trials, which he denies. Around 120 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial. According to witnesses, the movement denounced formal education as “satanic”, viewed modern medicine and hospitals as instruments of the devil and required followers to cut themselves off from the outside world. Mackenzie was arrested in April 2023 after a rights group alerted authorities and some followers were rescued from the 325-hectare (800-acre) ranch in the Shakahola forest on Kenya’s coast. The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights put the death toll at 429 in 2024. Some victims remain unidentified. nigeria.title: 2027: Obi couldn’t confront Anambra’s erosion, he lacks leadership traits — Tinubu
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has criticised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, over his handling of erosion in Anambra State, questioning his leadership qualities ahead of the 2027 general election. Tinubu spoke on Friday at the All Progressives Congress rally held at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, where he urged voters not to support Obi in the forthcoming presidential election. The President compared Obi’s record in Anambra with his own efforts to address coastal challenges in Lagos and those of Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno. “He’s in one party, they called NDC, who is running for President; he ran away from erosion in Anambra State. He could not confront erosion,” Tinubu said. “I, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I confronted the Atlantic Ocean, I tamed it for you. Umo Eno confronted the erosion in Akwa Ibom, and it’s working for you.” The President argued that Obi lacked the leadership qualities required to govern the country, citing his departure from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and subsequent move to the NDC. “They lack leadership character and traits,” Tinubu said. He questioned Obi’s decision to leave the PDP after previously being associated with the party, describing the move as evidence of a lack of political leadership. “If a man that once upon a time was a baby of PDP became a father of PDP and because of a little inconvenience he ran away from that party and formed a dangerous aide-de-camp in another party, is that a leadership trait? Is that a leadership character?” he asked. Tinubu further challenged Obi’s presidential ambition, telling supporters that the former Anambra governor was not fit to lead the country. “And he wants you to vote for him; it’s not for banana. He cannot put a house in order,” the President said. The rally formed part of Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom, where he inaugurated projects executed by the Eno administration before attending the APC political gathering. nigeria.title: Igbokoda Air Crash: NAF Retrieves Cockpit Voice Recorder As Search, Investigation Continue
nigeria.description: The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) on Friday said it has recorded further progress in the recovery and investigation of the ATR-42 aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, with the retrieval of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), which technical teams from the NAF and Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) have confirmed is intact. The Director of Public Relations and Information, Headquarters, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. According to him, part of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), also known as the black box, was recovered, while efforts to locate and retrieve its remaining portion are ongoing. He added that additional aircraft wreckage, engine components and human remains had also been recovered. Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa (5th-left) joined security agencies and other authorities at the crash site in search of the victims and the wreckage of the NAF aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State. The NAF said recovery operations were continuing in the challenging swamp terrain, with teams working to retrieve outstanding components and facilitate the necessary technical examinations. It noted that the investigation was being conducted with due diligence to ensure comprehensive and evidence-based findings. The Air Force added that the recovery process also involved careful handling of human remains, with the Directorate of Identification and Classification (DIC) undertaking the necessary procedures for proper identification. It said it had sustained engagements with the families of the victims, acknowledging their need for information and support. The NAF also said discussions with relevant authorities over environmental concerns raised by the host community remained an important part of its broader response. While appreciating the public’s concern and interest, the Air Force appealed for continued patience and understanding, noting that the critical processes required time, careful coordination and professional attention. “The ultimate objective is not only to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident but also to draw the necessary lessons to strengthen flight safety, enhance ongoing airpower operations and further safeguard the lives of personnel and citizens. “The NAF remains committed to providing verified updates as appropriate,” the statement added. The NAF ATR-42 aircraft, with tail number NAF 931, crashed in a swampy area near the Naval Base in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, on October 5, 2026. The aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin City, Edo State, to Lagos when air traffic controllers lost contact with it at about 9:13 a.m. The Air Force subsequently confirmed that all 25 people aboard, comprising 20 passengers and five crew members, died in the accident. nigeria.title: NDLEA remands two Mexicans, four Nigerians over Oyo meth lab
nigeria.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arraigned two Mexican nationals and four Nigerians over their alleged involvement in the establishment and operation of a clandestine methamphetamine laboratory in Tapa village, Ibarapa North Local Government Area of Oyo State. The six defendants were arraigned before Justice Nkeonye Evelyn Maha of the Federal High Court, Ibadan, on a four-count charge bordering on conspiracy, drug trafficking and the illegal production of methamphetamine. The NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. The defendants are 56-year-old Mexican, Jose Villa Ochoa; another Mexican, Carrera Loaiza Arturo, 40; and four Nigerians identified as Maxwell Uche Nevoh, 30; Olatunji Yusuf, 37; Bankole Akeem Owolabi, 45; and Ganiu Monsiu, 43. According to the statement, NDLEA operatives arrested Ochoa and the four Nigerian defendants on June 17, 2026, in a forested area of Tapa village, while Arturo was arrested on August 19, 2026, at the Lagos airport while allegedly attempting to flee the country. Babafemi said the four-count charge accused the defendants of conspiring to operate a drug trafficking organisation and establishing a clandestine laboratory for the production of methamphetamine between December 2025 and June 2026 at different locations in Lagos and Oyo states. They were also accused of unlawfully transporting and distributing chemical substances intended for the manufacture of methamphetamine, contrary to Section 20(1)(f) and punishable under Section 20(2)(a) of the NDLEA Act. All six defendants pleaded not guilty when the charges were read to them. Following their pleas, Justice Maha ordered that they be remanded at the Correctional Centre in Ibadan. The case was adjourned until January 26, 27, 28 and 29, 2027, for trial. The NDLEA spokesman also disclosed that three other Mexican nationals and seven Nigerians arrested over a similar alleged operation at a forest hideout in Ogun State on May 16, 2026, had been remanded following their arraignment before a Federal High Court in Lagos. He said the court had rejected their bail application and ordered an accelerated hearing of the case. nigeria.title: FG targets 2,000 new CNG facilities nationwide
nigeria.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government has announced plans to deploy about 2,000 additional Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) infrastructure units across the country to accelerate adoption of the alternative fuel and reduce transportation costs. Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (PI-CNG/EV), Ismaeel Ahmed, disclosed this on Friday shortly after the commissioning of a Rolling Energy CNG refuelling station for the State House in Karu, Abuja. Ahmed said Nigeria currently had about 160 operational CNG refuelling stations, while another 170 were at various stages of development or awaiting approval from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). He said the programme had moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage, with private investors committing about $2.6 billion to the development of CNG infrastructure. According to him, President Bola Tinubu has directed a fresh round of infrastructure expansion involving 1,500 units in February and another 500 in August through the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF). He said the additional facilities were expected to become operational between this year and early next year. “This is almost our 106th station across the country in less than two years. This is not beginning any longer. The market has been proven,” Ahmed said. He noted that Nigeria, with an estimated population of 220 million and about 12 million vehicles, needed to accelerate the deployment of refuelling facilities to meet growing demand. On the impact of CNG adoption on transportation costs, Ahmed said fares had dropped by between 30 and 40 per cent on routes where CNG-powered buses operate. He cited the Kano-Katsina route, where passengers who previously paid between N3,000 and N4,000 could now travel for about N1,500 using CNG-powered buses. “It has significantly reduced about 30 to 40 per cent of transportation fees in the routes where CNG buses are ferrying,” he said. The PI-CNG/EV chairman, however, acknowledged that existing facilities were inadequate to meet national demand, adding that the government was working to extend CNG-powered transportation to more commercial routes and underserved communities. Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Peter Fashedemi, said the commissioning of the facility demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to leading by example in adopting CNG as an alternative to petrol. He said the initiative had become particularly important following the removal of petrol subsidy, which increased transportation costs and made cheaper alternative fuels imperative. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review A final DOL rule that would ease alternative assets such as private equity, real estate and cryptocurrency into 401(k) retirement plans arrived at the White House on Thursday for review, Bloomberg Law reported , a procedural step that usually precedes public release. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged the package on Nov. 5 under the title “Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives,” RIN 1210-AC38. The filing lists the DOL’s Employee Benefits Security Administration as the authoring office, marks the stage as a final rule, flags it as economically significant and notes that there is no legal deadline for completion. The DOL unveiled the proposal on March 30. In that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding private assets to a 401(k) menu would get a legal safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The six factors named in the proposal are performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, performance benchmarks and complexity. Satisfying them does not force plans to offer crypto. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says Hackers tied to the record Binance theft have begun converting a large slice of the stolen XRP into bitcoin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in an update dated through Friday, with about 42 million XRP — roughly $50 million — already swapped, mostly through THORChain. Converted bitcoin from other stolen assets nearly doubled overnight to about 1,650 BTC, worth some $124 million, Elliptic wrote . Most of that jump came from the XRP route. About 192 million XRP, roughly $226 million, remained unswapped in addresses linked to the Binance theft. The XRP was part of the Oct. 29 drain that Binance later put at $6.34 billion. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC that day, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. The FBI has attributed the campaign to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion while covering customer losses from its own funds. How the XRP started moving The stolen XRP sat quiet at first. Early on Nov. 2, between 02:12 and 04:00 UTC, all about 233 million XRP moved into six new addresses, where it stayed until Nov. 5, Elliptic said . From the afternoon of Nov. 5, two of those six addresses began sending XRP on to dozens of new accounts that swapped it, mostly through THORChain into bitcoin. A small amount of ether also went through THORChain into bitcoin that evening. The main bitcoin and ether holdings from the theft — the largest pools — have still not moved, Elliptic said. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 economists expected, the Labor Department said Friday, and the bitcoin price briefly pushed above $76,100 before settling near $75,500, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, beating the Dow Jones forecast that called for it to hold. August payrolls moved to 186,000, an upward revision of 53,000, and September rose to 60,000 after a 31,000 upgrade, leaving the two-month total 84,000 stronger than first reported. The print lands on a market still digesting Thursday’s Nasdaq-led rout. The bitcoin price had held near $76,000 into that close, dipped toward $75,200 late in the session, then recovered into the mid-$75,000s overnight before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. The range on the day has run from about $75,240 to $76,280, leaving the market little changed from its pre-release level even as rate futures repriced. That muted finish fits the pattern after big macro prints. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Golfers Gain Distance By Fixing Attack Angle Numbers
sports.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Most avid golfers track their swing speed, yet many ignore the single metric that changes distance the most. Attack angle determines whether the club moves up or down at the moment of impact. This number dictates launch height and spin rates more than almost any other factor in the game. According to MyGolfSpy , a positive angle means the club moves upward, while a negative angle indicates a downward strike. The ideal number differs completely between the driver and irons, a fact that often confuses players who try to hit every club the same way. Understanding this distinction allows a golfer to maximize carry distance without increasing swing speed. MyGolfSpy reports that inconsistent attack angles can cause high-handicap players to see over 30 yards of carry variation. The same golfer with the same speed can hit shots 12 yards apart just by changing the angle of attack. This gap exists because the club path interacts with the ball differently depending on whether it is teed up or sitting on the turf. The Driver Requires an Upward Strike With the driver, the goal is to hit the ball on an upward strike. Golfers should tee the ball high and position it toward the front of the stance to facilitate this motion. MyGolfSpy explains that hitting up helps in two specific ways: it launches the ball higher and reduces spin. High launch combined with low spin creates the optimal conditions for maximum distance. sports.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The New York Mets just made a move that stings for Atlanta fans. The Mets are now stacking three hitting coaches in one room, a setup that feels strange for a team that needs immediate offense. A Familiar Name in a New Spot Washington is not a stranger to the Mets. Andy Green, the current Mets manager, previously employed him with the San Diego Padres and subsequently the Chicago Cubs. The hiring was reported by Joel Sherman of the New York Post, who noted the Mets finally have a new coach after weeks of searching. They fired their previous hitting coordinator, Jeff Albert, after just one season in the role. Washington joins Troy Snitker and Rafael Fernandez. The situation looks odd because the Mets missed out on top targets. Prior to selecting Washington, they consulted John Mallee of the Chicago Cubs and Kevin Long of the Philadelphia Phillies. Each was considered a top contender to direct the staff. Instead, the Mets turned to a familiar voice from Green’s past. This choice suggests they could not land the big names they wanted. The Braves, meanwhile, kept Tim Hyers as their hitting coach despite a lackluster offensive season. Why the Braves Let Him Go Braves fans have to ask why Washington slipped through their fingers. The team kept Hyers even though the offense ranked eighth in runs but had the third-fewest walks in MLB. Their on-base percentage of .309 was a full point lower than the Mets. In 2026, only the Colorado Rockies and San Francisco Giants posted a lower on-base rate than Atlanta. Washington would have signaled a change, but the Braves chose stability over a new voice. Washington’s past has its own baggage, though. He was the hitting coach for the Los Angeles Angels when they posted poor numbers. In 2024, the Angels batted .226 with him. Year two saw them hit .225. Before his Angels departure, a Reddit discussion noted an interview regarding his hitting philosophy. Critics labeled him a home run enthusiast who promoted a “wait for your pitch and end the at-bat” philosophy, according to Rising Apple . The Mets hired a coach with a mixed track record. The Mets cannot afford to repeat their offensive struggles from last season. They ranked in the bottom 10 in on-base percentage, slugging percentage, and runs scored. With Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto back healthy, the offense must improve. The Brewers had four hitting coaches last season and won the World Series. sports.description: American tennis star Jessica Pegula wasted little time defusing the tension around the well-documented "hot mic" incident during her appearance with media Friday ahead of the WTA Finals. As Pegula entered the room and sat down at the front of the press conference, she grabbed the microphone and playfully tapped it and said "OK, the mic's on. Just wanted to be sure." Her joke drew a laugh from the assembled media. Pegula was referencing an incident that happened earlier in the week when a microphone on the practice court that was intended to just pick up ambient noise of tennis balls hitting the hardcourt and environmental sounds for a livestream, actually picked up a conversation between Pegula and one of her coaches during a practice session. On the live stream she was heard calling another tour player Mirra Andreeva a "diva" among other comments in what she thought was a private discussion. A spokesperson for Pegula has since reported that Pegula "had absolutely no idea that her conversation with (her coach) was being livestreamed and certainly never expected a private discussion during practice to be made public." Pegula has since apologized to the other players involved. For its part, the WTA has taken full responsibility and apologized to Pegula for the incident. On Friday, WTA Chair Valerie Camillo, who spoke to the media minutes before Pegula did, struck a different tone that Pegula's light-hearted opener. She was quite serious. She said livestreaming practices is an attempt to bring fans closer to the game and they have done it before, using the similar ambient noise effect, but in this case mistakes were made. "There were several breakdowns in our execution of the livestream, given our own policies and procedures. There was a lack of advanced notice and clear signage to assist players about the recording equipment operating in the area and it was also not our intention to capture conversations on the livestream of practices but rather to record ambient sound. So clearly there was a failure in our technical execution. As the chair of the WTA I'm committed to leading an organization that delivers the best for our players, our tournaments and our fans. Our execution here did not meet that standard," she said. "I want to specifically apologize to Jessica Pegula, what happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest start and she does not deserve this distraction. One of the primary responsibilities of the WTA is to protect our players whenever possible. Camillo went on to say that the sound has been disabled now on the practice courts for the rest of this event. Nicco Marchiol, a left-handed transfer from West Virginia who has attempted one pass this season, is expected to make the start against an Iowa defense that ranks No. 4 nationally. Veteran back-up Nicco Marchiol will make the start for Northwestern, his first start for the Wildcats. He’s a veteran who has a 6-2 record as a starter while at West Virginia. He’s played in 27 career games. — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) November 6, 2026 The sudden move shifted the betting line.
